question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Pondicherry — Location & Foundation]
options: Pondicherry (Puducherry) is located on the Coromandel Coast of southeast India, facing the Bay of Bengal
Francois Martin founded Pondicherry in 1674, making it the capital of the French settlements in India
Pondicherry is situated on the Konkan Coast, directly facing the Arabian Sea
The French built Fort Louis at Pondicherry to defend their headquarters
wrong_fact: Pondicherry is NOT situated on the Konkan Coast facing the Arabian Sea. The Konkan Coast is on India's western side (Maharashtra/Goa). Pondicherry is on the eastern side (Tamil Nadu region) on the Coromandel Coast, facing the Bay of Bengal.
explanation: Puducherry (formerly Pondicherry) is on the Coromandel Coast in southeastern India, bordered by the state of Tamil Nadu. Francois Martin took charge of the French settlement in 1674 and developed it into the premier French administrative center in India. Fort Louis was constructed there. The Konkan Coast lies on the western side of the peninsula.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Pondicherry — Union Territory Enclaves & Geography]
options: The modern Union Territory of Puducherry comprises four non-contiguous districts: Puducherry, Karaikal, Yanam, and Mahe
Karaikal and Puducherry districts are coastal enclaves surrounded by Tamil Nadu
Yanam is an enclave situated on the Malabar Coast of Kerala, bordering the Arabian Sea
Mahe is a small enclave on the Malabar Coast of Kerala, bordering the Arabian Sea
wrong_fact: Yanam is NOT situated on the Malabar Coast of Kerala bordering the Arabian Sea. Yanam is a coastal enclave located on the eastern coast of India, near the mouth of the Godavari River, surrounded by the East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh (facing the Bay of Bengal).
explanation: The Union Territory of Puducherry consists of four scattered geographic enclaves: Puducherry and Karaikal (both on the Coromandel Coast, surrounded by Tamil Nadu); Yanam (on the East Coast at the Godavari delta, surrounded by Andhra Pradesh); and Mahe (on the Malabar Coast in southwest India, surrounded by Kerala).

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Pondicherry — Treaty of Ryswick & Geopolitical Control]
options: Pondicherry was captured by the Dutch in 1693 but restored to the French by the Treaty of Ryswick in 1697
During the First Carnatic War, La Bourdonnais launched a naval expedition from Mauritius to capture Madras, which was later returned to the English by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
In 1761, during the Third Carnatic War, the British captured and systematically destroyed the fortifications of Pondicherry
The Dutch captured Pondicherry in 1693 because the French garrison under Dupleix surrendered without a fight due to lack of supplies
wrong_fact: The French garrison in 1693 was NOT commanded by Dupleix, nor did he surrender it. Joseph François Dupleix was governor much later (1742–1754). In 1693, Pondicherry was commanded by Francois Martin, who surrendered it to the Dutch after a brief siege. It was later returned to France in 1697 under the Treaty of Ryswick.
explanation: Pondicherry's early colonial history involved Dutch occupation from 1693 to 1697, ended by the Treaty of Ryswick. François Martin was the governor at the time. Dupleix's era of influence was in the mid-18th century (during the Carnatic Wars). During the Carnatic Wars, Pondicherry was besieged and captured by the English under Eyre Coote in 1761, who razed the city's fortifications to the ground before it was restored to the French by the Treaty of Paris (1763).
